name: 6,7-Epoxymyrcene

papers.title: A Computational Examination of the Uncatalyzed Meinwald Rearrangement of Monoterpene Epoxides

research.basis: MeSH indexing and publication types of the most relevant PubMed records; counts are of papers in the sample, not findings.

vocabulary.structure: SEPIO assertion / evidence line / evidence item

consumer_summary.what_it_is: 6,7-Epoxymyrcene is an oxygen-containing terpene, a chemical cousin to the abundant plant volatile myrcene. As a monoterpene epoxide, it contributes to the complex aromatic profiles of certain herbs and spices, where people encounter it in tiny amounts as part of their essential oils.
consumer_summary.found_in: It has been identified in the essential oils of blue tansy (Tanacetum annuum), myoga ginger (Zingiber mioga), and the aromatic spice Zanthoxylum schinifolium.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Currently, 6,7-epoxymyrcene is primarily of interest to structural and computational chemists rather than medical researchers. Scientists are exploring how this molecule behaves and rearranges under different conditions, using chemical modeling (Oxford level 5, mechanistic evidence). Understanding these fundamental chemical properties helps researchers map out how plant volatiles degrade or transform in nature.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: The only available research consists of computational chemical modeling (Oxford level 5), with no biological or clinical studies yet conducted.

evidence: Measured in 2 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.07–0.08% of total volatiles (0.014–0.016mg per chew).
